What is the difference between an Osteopath and a Chiropractor?

I think: Historically chiropractors focused on the idea that all diseases could be cured by spinal manipulation. Osteopaths saw it all as bones (& muscles??). Modern day osteopath education is very similar to standard medical school; and chiropractors are excellent at spinal manipulation which can help/cure a number of musculo-skelatal issues.

The real comparison is allopathic physician vs. osteopathic physician. Allopathic focused more on treating the symptom - typically with medication. Osteopathic doctors treated the patient, and part of that treatment involved spinal manipulation. Osteopathic doctors, or D.O.s, still learn spinal manipulation while allopathic doctors, MDs, do not, however, both take the same USMLE certifications and go through boards.

Chiropractors are a great asset to the extremely few people who actually need them, but they seem to push their ideas and diagnosis on anyone who walks through their door. They have their own schools and certification path. Their main antithesis are physical therapists.
